title: After-hours call routing: How it works and how to set it up
summary: Want to keep up with incoming calls without sacrificing precious time off the clock? Learn how to set up after-hours call routing.
body_markdown:
You *finally* clock out on a Friday night, and you’re excited to put your feet up. Then a potential customer calls. Normally, you’d pick up, but you’re trying to silence calls after closing time for better work-life balance. Eventually, the call goes to voicemail.


Unfortunately, most callers won’t leave a message. Many try the next business on their list and work with a competitor instead. The caller in our example might do the same.


So, how do you capture leads without sacrificing your hard-won time off?


The answer is to use after-hours call routing.


This article explains what after-hours call routing is and provides options for handling these calls. You’ll also see a few call flow examples in action and learn the step-by-step process to set them up in Quo’s phone platform.


##


Key takeaways


- Voicemail alone loses leads. Only about 15% of callers leave a voicemail, so combine a phone menu, an answering option, and a plan for urgent calls into a single after-hours call flow.
- An after-hours call routing plan sends after-hours calls to a person, phone number, or AI receptionist, so every caller gets a next step.


-


- An AI receptionist like Sona can answer calls 24/7, capture lead details, and transfer urgent calls. Use a call flow builder to build your own call flow in 15 minutes or less.


##


**What is after-hours call routing?**


After-hours call routing is a set of time-based routing rules in your phone system. It automatically routes calls that come in outside of business hours to a different destination, depending on the rules you set. For example, you might send after-hours calls to your voicemail inbox or let an AI receptionist triage them for you.


### **How after-hours call routing works**


After-hours call routing works by following rules you set to send callers to a specific destination, such as a person, phone number, or AI agent.


1. Set your business hours, including your time zone, in your phone system. In Quo’s[call flow](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-flow/) builder, for instance,[adding business hours](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/administration/call-flows/business-hours) automatically splits your call flow into “During” and “After” hours paths.
2. Your phone system checks each incoming call against those hours.
3. Calls outside of business hours follow your after-hours path to whatever destination you choose. Advanced tools like Quo can even check *who’s* calling and route calls based on that.


The best call routing systems also let you create temporary or scheduled call flows. With those, you can set up custom schedules for holidays, weekends, or emergencies that override your normal schedule.


##


**3 Benefits your team unlocks with after-hours call routing**


In most industries, less than[one in four](https://www.quo.com/blog/why-callers-dont-leave-voicemail/) callers leave a voicemail. Having a plan for after-hours calls can help you connect with more people and drive more revenue.


### **1. Fewer missed calls and lost customers**


Without routing capabilities, your after-hours callers must wait for voicemail. Since most callers don’t leave messages, this could lead to lost revenue.


In Quo’s analysis of over 18 million missed calls, only[~15% of callers](https://www.quo.com/blog/why-callers-dont-leave-voicemail/) left a voicemail. It doesn’t help that a missed call from a new lead is often a lost job or sale. The benefit of routing is that it gives every caller a next step, even if it’s just an automated message telling them when you’ll call back.


### **2. Urgent calls still reach your on-call staff**


After-hours routing lets you sort urgent calls from routine questions, so emergencies don’t have to wait until the next morning.


For example, an appliance company can ask callers to “Press one for emergencies,” which forwards the call to whoever’s working late. This works even if the on-call person uses their own cell, since you can forward the call to an outside number.


Once you set this up, callers can get immediate help if their washer leaks. Everything else goes to voicemail or an AI receptionist until your team can follow up.


### **3. Your team gets time off**


[Routing](https://quo.com/product/call-routing) protects your team’s evenings and weekends. That way, their phones only ring for calls that truly can’t wait.


With a routing system like Quo, you can tap into tools like business hours, work schedules, and Do Not Disturb. This lets team members mute notifications outside of working hours. Now, you can provide after-hours coverage without overextending your team.


##


**3 Best practices for better after-hours call handling**


Most businesses need more than one tool to handle after-hours calls. Depending on your business, you’ll likely need to combine a phone menu, an answering option, and a plan for urgent calls in one after-hours call flow.


### **1. Set up a phone menu so callers can route themselves**


An after-hours[phone menu](https://www.quo.com/blog/phone-menu/) , also known as an interactive voice response menu, or IVR, greets callers with an automated message and lets them choose where their calls go. For example, your IVR might tell callers to “Press one for emergencies,” “Press two for new inquiries,” or “Press three for business hours and location details.”


In Quo, each phone menu option can route to Sona, forward to another number, play audio, or go to voicemail. Quo also supports multi-level menus if your callers need more choices.


The biggest benefit of an IVR menu is that callers can route themselves to the right place without anyone answering the phone. Plus, recorded options for business hours and directions answer routine questions on their own, and phone menus help filter out spam calls.


You can learn more about[intelligent call routing](https://www.quo.com/blog/intelligent-call-routing/) in our guide.


That said, keep in mind that phone menus only offer *fixed options* . They can’t answer questions or take action. They’re usually best when paired with other solutions, like practices two and three on this list.


### **2. Decide if and when calls should reach a person after hours**


Not every business needs someone on-call 24/7. For example, most law firms and retail businesses don’t usually deal with genuine emergencies. But an HVAC or plumbing company may have callers in situations that require an immediate response.


With after-hours call routing, you can handle every kind of emergency by quickly sending people to the right destinations. For example, you could use a phone menu option to forward urgent calls to on-call staff at an external number, like a technician’s cell. Or you could choose to create a short list of VIP clients who should always reach a member of your team.


Everyone else goes to Sona or voicemail so you can follow up with non-urgent calls later.


### **3. Route after-hours calls to capture leads**


If calls from new leads go to voicemail, as you know, you’ll probably lose them. So, you’ll need some *one* or some *thing* available to answer.


There are two primary ways to do this: with an AI receptionist or with a live[after-hours answering service](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/after-hours-answering-service) . You can always use voicemail as a fallback if anything goes awry.


Here’s a quick comparison chart of these options:


Option Availability Best for Main drawback Price


AI receptionist 24/7, including weekends and holidays Routine calls like FAQs, lead capture, and booking links Can struggle with complex or sensitive calls 10 AI handled calls included with tools like Quo’s Sona, up to $250 per month or higher for bundled minutes


Live after-hours answering service Up to 24/7 coverage, depending on add-on costs High-value or sensitive calls where callers expect a person, like legal intake Per-minute billing can make monthly costs unpredictable From $75 to $1,500+ flat fee per month, $1 to $11 per call, or $1.49 to $2.99 per minute


Voicemail 24/7, but no live pickups or greetings Low-stakes calls from existing customers, or as a fallback Many callers hang up without leaving a message, so you may lose leads Usually included in your phone plan


#### **AI receptionists**


AI voice agents like Sona answer every call 24/7 using natural-sounding language. With Sona, you can capture every lead’s contact information with intake questions you define. Our[AI answering service](https://www.quo.com/answering-service) also answers routine calls about hours, services, and pricing from your knowledge base. It can even text callers a booking link mid-call to schedule appointments.


Each Sona call comes with a summary and transcription. It can also automatically sync with CRM integrations like HubSpot, Salesforce, and Jobber. This ensures your team can follow up in the morning without piecing together all the context on their own.


Of course, an[AI receptionist](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/receptionist) can’t handle *every* request. When it can’t, it takes a message for a human to follow up, so you still have a chance to convert new leads.


#### **Live after-hours answering services**


A live after-hours service refers to a human receptionist who answers calls on your behalf. Providers like Posh, Ruby, and Smith.ai all offer[human answering services for small businesses](https://www.quo.com/blog/answering-service-for-small-business/) .


Human agents can offer a real human voice, which may be a good fit for sensitive or complex calls. The drawback is that it’s usually the most expensive option, often with extra charges for after-hours coverage. You also need to worry about:


- Callers waiting in call queues during busy periods
- Long setup times because the service needs scripts and requires training
- Call details that live outside your phone system


That said, you can mitigate a few of these issues by using Quo as your business phone system. You can forward after-hours calls to an external live answering service number, for example. This keeps call details within your phone system.


#### **Standard voicemail**


Using voicemail alone will cost you leads after hours. Remember: just 15% of missed calls result in a voicemail at all. Plus, it may take a while for you to call them back yourself. Our own data found[69% of missed business calls](https://www.quo.com/blog/small-business-callback-statistics/) don’t get a callback within 48 hours.


One way to fix this in Quo is to turn on[voicemail-to-email](https://www.quo.com/blog/voicemails-to-email/) and automatic transcriptions. That way, you can quickly catch up on missed messages without worrying about them going unread.


You could also send an automated text after a missed call, so callers know when to expect a reply.


You can learn more about this in our guide to[missed call text back software](https://www.quo.com/blog/missed-call-text-back-software/) .


##


**3 Examples of after-hours call flows**


The “best” after-hours setup depends on what your callers need.


To help you make the most informed decision, we’ll look at three short step-by-step call flows — each of which can be built in Quo’s call flow builder.


### **1. A home services business with an emergency line**


Let’s say you’re a[home services](https://www.quo.com/solutions/home-services) company that often gets emergency calls at night. To help these callers after hours, you could:


- Play a greeting with your hours, so callers know when to call back.
- If they call and don’t leave a message, send an auto-reply text to confirm your team will follow up in the morning.
- Set up an IVR phone menu. If callers press one for emergencies, their call forwards to the on-call technician’s number. If callers press two, they route to Sona to ask questions or leave a message.


One Quo customer, Southern Hills Appliance Repair, uses a similar flow to help triage incoming calls. Owner Carl Jarvis explains what they did: *“\[We\] loaded Sona’s knowledge with a database of error codes. When a caller specifically reads out an E6 on their dishwasher, Sona checks it against the database for that model, explains that it’s most likely a leak error, and tells them someone should come out to fix it right away. A booking link follows by text.”*


You can read more about this in[our dedicated playbook](https://www.quo.com/blog/appliance-repair-call-routing/) .


### **2. A professional services firm capturing new leads**


If you manage a professional services company, like a law firm or accounting office, most of your after-hours callers are likely new leads rather than emergencies. One way to handle this is to route all after-hours calls straight to Sona. You can do this with the following call flow:


- Sona asks callers intake questions you define. These questions could include the caller’s name, reason for calling, and preferred callback time.
- You can have Sona text a booking link if a caller requests to schedule an appointment. That way, callers can book an appointment automatically without speaking with your team.
- You’ll get a call summary and transcript for each Sona call in Quo. You can sync these to your CRM, so your team has the context they need to manage future interactions.


### **3. A team spread across time zones**


Let’s say you run a remote team or[multi-location](https://www.quo.com/blog/multi-location-phone-systems/) business where “after hours” varies by person. To create an after-hours call flow, you can:


- Set business hours in your main time zone.
- Have team members set work schedules so calls only ring whoever is on shift.
- Calls go to Sona or to voicemail with voicemail-to-email turned on if everybody is off.


This can help keep calls from disrupting off-duty teammates in other time zones. It also improves the likelihood that your caller will reach the right person at the right time.


### How to set up after-hours call routing with Quo

With Quo, you can set up an after-hours[call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing) workflow in 15 minutes or less. Just use our visual, drag-and-drop call flow builder to get started — no technical skills required.

Business hours, the call flow builder, and our AI agent Sona are available on all plans. We recommend the Business or Scale plan if you want phone menus or advanced call forwarding.

Next, invite your teammates in the app by adding their email addresses. You can also have them set their work schedules if you plan to route calls by shift.


### **3. Set your business hours**


Go to **Settings** and **Phone numbers** , select your number, and toggle **Enable business hours.**


Now, you can choose your time zone and set your schedule type. You can set the same hours for each day, build in weekends, or set different hours for each day of the week.


### **4. Build your during- and after-hours paths in the call flow builder**


Open the call flow builder from your number’s settings. Then drag the **Business hours** step in after the **Incoming call** trigger. This will create “during hours” and “after hours” paths that your system will route callers through.


On the **After hours** path, add the steps you wish for callers to interact with first. This could be:


- A phone menu
- Forwarding a call
- Sending callers to voicemail
- Playing an audio recording
- Routing callers to Sona


You may want to turn on voicemail transcriptions and email notifications to know if and when callers miss your team. Or you can set up after-hours auto-replies so callers get a text when you miss their call.


### **5. Schedule call flows for holidays**


Next, you can create alternate call flows and schedule them in advance for out-of-the-ordinary events.


You can do this quickly by setting a start time, like December 24, and choosing which flow takes over afterward. That way, nobody has to remember to switch the routing back manually when they’re back in the office.


### **6. Test and adjust your call flows**


The last step is to test your call flow by calling your number outside of business hours. This lets you hear what callers hear and make any necessary edits or tweaks.


You should also train your AI voice agent to handle customer requests more efficiently. For example, you could review Sona’s call summaries and transcriptions in Quo. Then, update Sona’s knowledge base or phone menu based on what callers ask or what gaps might be missing.

##


**FAQs**


****How do business hours work?****


Business hours tell your phone system when you’re open. When calls come in outside those hours, the system automatically follows your after-hours routing plan. With Quo, you can set hours for every phone number in your time zone, then set up[Sona for lead capture](https://support.quo.com/core-concepts/ai-automations/sona/sona-sms) or auto-replies for after-hours texts.


****Can I forward after-hours calls to my cell phone?****


Yes. You can forward after-hours calls to your cell phone by adding a **Forwarding** step to your **After-hours path** in Quo. However, if you’re using the Quo mobile app, you don’t need call forwarding because you can take business calls on your cell without forwarding the number. You’ll keep your personal number private without switching between devices.


****How much does an after-hours answering service cost?****


Live answering services like Posh typically charge for bundles of minutes or calls. Others require a monthly base price, per-minute fees, and add-ons for after-hours coverage. Keep in mind that AI[answering services typically cost](https://www.quo.com/blog/answering-service-cost/) much less than live services, since you’re not paying a human to staff your phones late at night.


****Can a virtual receptionist handle after-hours calls?****


Yes. Both human and AI[virtual receptionists](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-a-virtual-receptionist/) can handle after-hours calls. Just know that humans might cost extra for after-business-hours support. AI virtual receptionists like Sona, on the other hand, can answer 24/7 without add-on costs.


****How do I set up holiday hours for my phone system?****


In Quo, you can create a temporary call flow with a custom holiday greeting, then automatically switch back to your regular flow afterward. Just add an after-hours automated message by text, so callers know when you’ll reopen. This sets the right expectations while you’re off the clock.
